blocks.content: Intraplate earthquakes occur in the interior of a tectonic plate, far from plate boundaries, often reactivating ancient zones of weakness.

rows: Within the interior of tectonic plates
Reactivation of ancient crustal faults under localized stress
Deccan Trap / Peninsular region (e.g., 1993 Latur, 2001 Bhuj)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Intraplate earthquakes occur within the interior of a tectonic plate rather than along active plate margins.
Peninsular India, traditionally regarded as a Stable Continental Region (SCR), is susceptible to destructive intraplate seismic activity.
These quakes are primarily caused by the reactivation of pre-existing ancient zones of weakness under compressive intraplate stresses.
Notable Indian intraplate earthquakes include Koyna (1967), Latur (1993), and Bhuj (2001).
Due to long recurrence intervals, intraplate seismic hazard assessment remains a critical challenge for disaster mitigation.
Distinguish between Interplate (Himalayan boundary zone) and Intraplate (Peninsular Shield) seismic zones for UPSC Geography.
Koyna earthquake (1967) is a classic example of Reservoir-Induced Seismicity (RIS) in an intraplate setup.
Focus on the 'Stable Continental Region (SCR)' concept and strain accumulation driven by the northward drift of the Indian Plate.
